reasons: coarse plan for the V: the engine is one big item (three files, about 60 tests) that the squad divides itself, test-first, with the parent kept as an integrating coordinator
the page is decoupled from the engine (evaluate is injected), so it runs beside the engine

items.title: Engine tests
items.goal: Write tests for the calculator expression engine before it exists

card.context: A developer will implement the engine against your tests, so they must be correct and specific.
card.contract: src/calc.js exports evaluate(expr, options) returning a number. expr is a string; options.degrees (boolean, default false) makes sin cos tan take degrees and asin acos atan return degrees. Operators: + - * / % ^ (right associative; binds tighter than unary minus, so -2^2 is -4), postfix ! (factorial), parentheses, unary + and -. Numbers: 12, 1.5, .5, 1.5e2. Constants: pi e tau. One-argument functions: sin cos tan asin acos atan sinh cosh tanh ln log (base 10) log2 sqrt cbrt abs exp floor ceil round fact. Two-argument functions: pow min max. Invalid input must throw an Error: division or modulo by zero, unknown names or functions, wrong argument count, sqrt of a negative, unbalanced parentheses, a trailing operator, unexpected characters.
acceptance: uses node:test and node:assert/strict and imports { evaluate } from '../src/calc.js'
at least 10 test cases: operators, precedence, ^ associativity, factorial, decimals, constants, radians and degrees, logs, two-argument functions, error cases
floating point results are compared with a tolerance of 1e-9, never with strict equality
tests do not depend on each other

items.title: Page tests
items.goal: Write tests for the calculator page's behaviour using the harness fake DOM and an injected evaluate function

card.context: A developer will build the page against your tests. The fake DOM replaces a browser.
card.contract: src/ui.js exports mount(document, evaluate). evaluate(expr, { degrees }) is passed in by the caller (the page passes the real engine; your tests pass a fake such as (e, o) => 42, and one that throws new Error('bad input')). ui.js must not import the engine. It uses #expr (input, .value), #result (output, .textContent), #degrees (checkbox, .checked) and every button[data-key] from document.querySelectorAll('button[data-key]'). Clicking a button appends its data-key to #expr.value, except: 'C' clears #expr and #result; 'DEL' removes the last character of #expr; '=' evaluates #expr.value with evaluate(value, { degrees: #degrees.checked }) (the injected function) and sets #result.textContent to the number, or to 'Error: ' + message if it throws. A keydown event with key 'Enter' on #expr also evaluates. The harness file tests/helpers/dom-stub.mjs exports createDom() returning { document, expr, result, degrees, buttons, press(key), keydown(key) }.
acceptance: imports createDom from './helpers/dom-stub.mjs' and mount from '../src/ui.js', and uses node:test and node:assert/strict
at least 6 tests: building an expression, equals calls the injected evaluate with the expression and the degrees flag, clear, delete, error display, the Enter key, degrees mode
each test creates its own dom with createDom() and calls mount(dom.document, fakeEvaluate)
do not read index.html (another item tests the page)

items.title: Page tests
items.goal: Write tests for index.html and style.css before they exist

card.context: A developer will write the page against your tests. They read files only; no browser is involved.
card.contract: index.html must contain: an element with id expr (input), id result (output) and id degrees (checkbox input), and a <button data-key="KEY"> for every key in: 0-9 . + - * / % ^ ( ) ! pi e sin( cos( tan( asin( acos( atan( ln( log( sqrt( C DEL = (the keys written as data-key values, e.g. data-key="sin(" and data-key="="); a <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">; and an inline <script type="module"> that imports { evaluate } from './src/calc.js' and { mount } from './src/ui.js' and calls mount(document, evaluate). style.css must exist and be non-empty. Read the files with node:fs and path from the project root: new URL('../index.html', import.meta.url).
acceptance: uses node:test and node:assert/strict and node:fs only
at least 6 test cases: each id, every key button present (loop over the key list), the stylesheet link, the module script wiring, style.css non-empty
tests do not depend on each other

items.title: Calculator page script
items.goal: Implement src/ui.js so the provided tests pass

card.context: Replace the stub src/ui.js. The engine is injected, so you do not need it: the tests pass a fake.
card.contract: export function mount(document, evaluate): wire the page as the tests describe. Use #expr (input, .value), #result (output, .textContent), #degrees (checkbox, .checked) and every button[data-key] from document.querySelectorAll('button[data-key]'). A click appends the button's data-key to #expr.value, except 'C' clears #expr and #result, 'DEL' removes the last character, and '=' calls evaluate(#expr.value, { degrees: #degrees.checked }) and sets #result.textContent to Number(value.toPrecision(12)) as text, or 'Error: ' + message if it throws. A keydown event with key 'Enter' on #expr also evaluates. Do not import anything and do nothing at import time: the page calls mount(document, evaluate).

items.title: Calculator page markup and style
items.goal: Write index.html and style.css so the provided page tests pass and it works in a browser

card.context: Replace the stub index.html and add style.css. The tests below are the specification.
card.contract: index.html: <input id="expr">, <output id="result">, <input type="checkbox" id="degrees"> with a label, a <button data-key="KEY">KEY</button> for each key in: 0-9 . + - * / % ^ ( ) ! pi e sin( cos( tan( asin( acos( atan( ln( log( sqrt( C DEL =, <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">, and <script type="module">import { evaluate } from './src/calc.js'; import { mount } from './src/ui.js'; mount(document, evaluate);</script>. style.css: a simple readable calculator layout (a grid of buttons, a large result), no frameworks.
acceptance: the page works in a browser served by node serve.mjs

items.title: Expression engine
items.goal: Implement the expression engine so the provided tests pass

card.context: Replace the stub src/calc.js with a real implementation; the tests below are the specification.
card.contract: export function evaluate(expr, options = {}) returning a number; options.degrees switches trig functions to degrees. Support + - * / % ^ (right associative, tighter than unary minus), postfix !, parentheses, constants pi e tau, functions sin cos tan asin acos atan sinh cosh tanh ln log log2 sqrt cbrt abs exp floor ceil round fact, and pow min max. Throw an Error with a clear message on any invalid input. The code may be split over src/calc.js (parser and evaluator, exports evaluate), src/lexer.js (tokenizer) and src/functions.js (math functions, constants, factorial).
acceptance: plain ES module, no dependencies, no eval() and no new Function()
notes: Output src/calc.js, and src/lexer.js and src/functions.js if you split it
